affectedPublicSurfaces: no public surface; the analytics_backfill_topup Celery beat task only

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: worker-only change; no candidate HTTP route required

journeys.name: a-failure-record-survives-the-run-that-created-it
journeys.entryUrl: worker: trigger analytics_backfill_topup once on the deployed sha
assertions: at least one row in ops.analytics_backfill_partitions has updated_at AFTER the deploy timestamp
attempt_count on a previously-failed row is strictly greater than its pre-deploy value
last_error is a real exception string, not the literal 'LIVE partition failed'

journeys.name: the-1668-guarantee-still-holds
assertions: zero PendingRollbackError in the worker journal for that run
partitions continue to run after the first failure rather than cascading

journeys.name: 1672-can-finally-act
assertions: a partition whose error carries 401/403/404 is committed with retryable=false

htmlRoutes: not-applicable: worker-only change, no HTML route

migrationCompatibility.notes: No schema change. Writes to ops.analytics_backfill_partitions use columns that already exist; the change is transaction ordering, not shape. Stable and candidate can run concurrently against the same table.

rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: revert to fbc7ef1c; the task returns to discarding failure records, which is the pre-existing behaviour and loses no committed data

doNotInfer: Do not claim this removes the analytics_backfill_topup timeout — it makes the real failures observable; the three persistence bugs behind them are separate issues
Do not treat the 75 already-mis-marked rows as repaired — they need one run to be re-attempted and correctly re-marked
Do not read a run that completes without raising as evidence — the failure mode this fixes was a successful no-op that recorded nothing (ADR-089 evidence standard)
Do not revert #1668's rollback while fixing its side effect — the cascade it prevents was observed in production twice
